I’m driving, and there is a pop up blocking the screen, and pushing “no” pulls up an even bigger pop up with like 5 choices on it. And the cancel button is in small print at the bottom. I’m driving, the app knows I’m driving, and it’s trying to get me to interact with it in a way that would completely consume my attention. Do the developers even drive? Please fix your app, and I’ll give it a second try. I do like your current pricing. But it ain’t worth it the way the app is now.

title: Very dissapointed
body: I am a truck driver with more than 20 years driving experience. I am also a self taught IT guy so i am very familiar with software development and related fields. This software is AMATEUR-ish at best. Besides the fact that it takes into account routing for Class 8 trucks, its features are way below any cheap general GPS unit on the market. I made the mistake and paid $65 for a piece of crap. I read the other " positive" reviews but i strongly doubt they are from legitimate truck drivers. This amateur software has no 3D navigation mode. It only display a Bird Eye view and is very confusing at showing turns and freeway exits and merges especially when the road splits out into multiple lanes and into multiple freeway junctions. This is because the upcoming turn or merge or split is OFF the screen and many times it comes into view AFTER you pass the exit or merge or split. So far i still have to trust my old Tom Tom trusty GPS unit for this kind of navigation. Another annoying flaw is that many a times, the software will go into Search Mode showing the spinning wheel right into the middle of navigation making you miss important turns or exits or merges. And this happens even in major metropolitan areas with excellent 3G or 4G coverage. Forget using this crappy software if you are in a rural area and you want to start and input a new route, this crap doesn't even know where it is. Another major flaw is while navigating surface streets in major metropolitan areas. The software will go into refresh-search mode for quite a few good seconds (20-30 at least as installed on my iPhone) leaving you wonder where to go and turn next. Imagine being in New York City or Chicago trying to avoid low underpasses and restricted streets. Not only that but after the software finds itself , it shows you few turns back, turns that you already had been through leaving you completely confused about where you are . The Voice this software uses is really pathetic. It sounds like some drunken guy mumbling unintelligible gibberish. Do not expect to hear it without uising it through your truck speakers at very loud volume in order to make up the spoken directions. Another major left out feature is the zooming in prior to approaching splits, merges and turns, not to mention the lack of real turn graphics. The software does some zooming in but it usually happens much to late when you already are past the moment of taking the decision of which way to go. It would only be ok if one would drive at walking speed then you would probably have enough time to watch the GPS and see which way it wants you to go. When you approach any turn the voice says: Approach turn on the left. It always says LEFT regardless if you will turn left or right. It will say the right direction at the following warning. If you are a real truck driver, my advice is to stay away from this software. The developers probably have no idea about real word truck driving so really how can they develop software helpful to a truck driver ? I am using a Tom Tom unit, i bought and returned the truck version units from Rand McNally and Cobra which i found full of flaws and errors. Garmin would be the best so far but still my Tom Tom is infinitely more customizable even if it is just an automobile designed unit. I am also using the GPS Truck CoPilot software on my iPhone which is infinitely much better software compared to this. It also loads the whole map in the memory so you can start a new route even if you are without any cellular signal. So until all these issues are going to be addressed by these city slickers developers, with forced generosity i will award you with one star. I really have no preferences as far as brands, i am just looking for the software that will best help me the best at navigating a big truck. Sorry to say this one does not even come close. I am just looking forward to get home now and to my computer to access iTunes and demand a refund.

title: Navigation is Great for Drivers!!!
body: This app works great if you're a truck driver that has a smartphone or tablet and don't want to spend 200-500 bucks on a gps in a store. I'm OTR and use this app for all of my p/u & deliveries. It hasn't taken me down a non-truck route yet ! No low bridges or sketchy residential areas anymore just gives you multiple options in your route plan. Like quickest or shortest route for trucks, shows truck stops, weigh stations (it notifies you 7 miles prior to), and much more. I would definitely recommend it !!!

title: Excellent app for truckers!!!!
body: I have been using this app religiously for a year now with an iPhone 6 Plus and have found it to be very accurate. I prefer an American sounding female voice over it's British counterpart for the navigation. It also uses 45 gigs of memory so make sure you have enough before attempting a download. I love the truckstop option and the DOT scales within 7 miles option showing you those points of interest along your route. I'm giving it five stars for its accuracy and functionality. I like being able to search by company name just like google instead of address only on the more expensive stand alone gps units sold in truck stops. Overall, it is a very useful app which I am well pleased, it has been a blessing to me.
